page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-224 is a high-capacity compute instance engineered for memory-intensive enterprise applications. Operating on the 64-bit x86 architecture, the instance provides 224 dedicated vCPUs paired with 5952 GB of system memory. This architecture yields a memory ratio of 26.57 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing the instance at the extreme end of memory-dense cloud infrastructure.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage entirely, requiring deployments to rely on external network-attached storage for root volumes, databases, and persistent data tiers. The system includes zero GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its operational focus exclusively toward CPU-based execution and in-memory operations within private cloud networks.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the server addresses workloads that cannot be partitioned across multiple distributed nodes. While operating at a premier resource tier, cost efficiency is realized through vertical consolidation, removing inter-node communication latency and the synchronization overhead of distributed clusters. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete reliance on network storage for cold starts, bulk data loading, and snapshotting.

Workload applicability centers on enterprise in-memory computing. The massive 5.95 TB memory footprint is suited for large-scale SAP HANA deployments, massive in-memory transactional databases, extensive distributed cache consolidation, real-time telemetry processing, and large in-memory graph analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-224 is an ultra-high-memory compute instance designed for enterprise scale-up computing. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, the server features 224 dedicated vCPUs and 5952 GB of RAM, providing a substantial ratio of 26.57 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing all persistent disk operations to network-attached block storage. The m4n-ultramem-224 provides economic efficiency for monolithic architectures by eliminating the networking and clustering overhead associated with multi-node scale-out configurations. Storage throughput and network bandwidth are critical operational factors due to the absence of local disks and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This system is purpose-built for massive in-memory databases, including large SAP HANA deployments, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching layers, and high-volume enterprise resource planning systems.
